request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I create a search field with modelOptions: { updateOn: "blur", debounce: 250 }. Is that the right shape and will it configure a control I supply myself?
required_points: Use debounce: { default: 250 }.
updateOn accepts change/blur/submit and is passed at new-control construction.
Do not promise reconfiguration of supplied existing controls.
forbidden_claims: A bare debounce number is supported.
An existing control always has updateOn rewritten.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I set updateOn: "submit" and debounce: { default: 300 } expecting Formly to delay validation and my HTTP calls by 300ms. What does this actually control?
required_points: The debounce branch requires absent/change updateOn and positive default.
It delays Formly assignment/event propagation, not an HTTP scheduler or a promise about validation timing.
forbidden_claims: Submit uses this debounce branch.
Formly debounces validators and HTTP requests.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My two parsers trim and uppercase an account code, but I need the control to retain the original text. Does Formly normalize only the model?
required_points: Parsers run in order with chained results.
A changed parsed result is written back to the control.
Do not promise raw control text preservation; repeated emissions require stable normalization.
forbidden_claims: Parsers only modify the model.
Every custom widget preserves the typed text.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: After adding modelOptions: { debounce: { default: 250 } } my uppercase parser stopped normalizing a search code. Is the parser guaranteed to run before the delay, including the initial value?
required_points: With absent/change updateOn the positive debounce branch replaces rather than extends the parser pipeline.
It bypasses parsers and the earlier distinct/startWith steps.
Do not infer a fix or the same behavior for a different release.
forbidden_claims: Parsers always run before debounce.
The debounced branch preserves initial startWith.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: I subscribe to control.valueChanges and read the root model immediately. Should I treat that as the same event as options.fieldChanges? What about a keyless display control?
required_points: These are distinct surfaces; the Formly leaf path assigns keyed model value before fieldChanges.
Keyless leaf controls emit without keyed assignment.
Do not promise arbitrary control subscribers observe the completed root model.
forbidden_claims: All valueChanges surfaces are interchangeable.
A keyless field always writes a root-model property.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: For autosave, is modelChange just the field scalar and does it fire once per control emission before expressions run?
required_points: modelChange emits a Formly clone of the host model after expression checking.
It consumes keyed fieldChanges valueChanges; zone stability and switchMap prevent a universal one-to-one timing guarantee.
forbidden_claims: modelChange emits only the changed scalar.
It always emits before expression checks.
It guarantees one emission per keystroke.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My custom widget calls props.change(field, event), but its selected value never reaches the model. Is the callback the value accessor?
required_points: No: the directive handler invokes the callback and marks dirty.
It does not set the value; supply the appropriate control/value accessor integration.
forbidden_claims: Calling props.change updates the Formly model automatically.
Programmatic setValue must invoke every renderer props.change.

request: My application uses Formly 7 with Material. Can you guarantee that these parser, debounce and modelChange contracts apply unchanged?
required_points: The available exact-6.3.12 knowledge does not establish release-7 behavior.
State the version coverage gap rather than asserting compatibility.
forbidden_claims: These behaviors are verified for Formly 7.

request: I use Formly 6.3.12 with Bootstrap. Please certify the complete Bootstrap widget interaction and browser rendering behavior from your Material/core sources.
required_points: Core implementation evidence does not certify Bootstrap renderer/browser interaction.
State the adapter qualification gap.
forbidden_claims: Material/core source certifies complete Bootstrap browser behavior.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: My parser appends an exclamation mark on every call. Does Formly guarantee it will run exactly once for a change?
required_points: Parser output is written back if not Object.is-equal to the control.
Write-back can emit again; use stable/idempotent normalization.
forbidden_claims: It is guaranteed to run once.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: With updateOn: "blur" and debounce: { default: 250 }, is the parser bypassed by the positive debounce branch?
required_points: The debounce replacement requires absent/change updateOn.
Blur does not enter that branch; do not conflate blur timing with a 250ms Formly debounce.
forbidden_claims: Every positive debounce bypasses parsers even with blur.

request: In a Material application using Formly 6.3.12: A keyless leaf emits fieldChanges valueChanges. Does that guarantee formly-form modelChange is emitted from this event?
required_points: The leaf can emit without assigning a keyed value.
The host filters for hasKey(field), so the keyless event does not satisfy this host filter.
forbidden_claims: Every keyless leaf event triggers host modelChange.
